To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the optimization of microvessel enrichment and sample preparation methods is essential to the identification and quantification BBB transporters in isolated brain microvessles.

the optimization of isolation of rat brain capillaries and enrichment of endothelial proteins was achieved by using a novel isolation protocol, and a combination of label‐free and targeted proteomics was adopted for quantification of BBB transporter proteins.
the combination of targeted proteomics, untargeted proteomics, and transcriptomics can be used for the quantification of transporters in the blood‐brain barrier.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the make‐up and function of the rat blood–brain barrier.
the development of experimental approaches for the identification and quantification, using both targeted and untargeting approaches, of BBB transporters in isolated microvessel endothelial cells.
the optimization of experimental workflows for isolation, enrichment, and quantification of rat brain microvascular endothelial proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methods described herein provide a robust platform for the identification and quantification for proteins of the blood‐brain barrier in the rat.

the workflow presented in this study provides an excellent starting point to investigate BBB transporters in rat brain microvessel isolation and proteomic analysis, and can be adapted to other species.

this study has demonstrated the feasibility of the use of the described workflows in the identification, quantification, and validation of BBB proteins in isolated rat brain capillary endothelial cells, as well as the potential for their use in the translation of BBB transporter‐based pharmacological and toxicokinetic observations into humans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of optimized microvessel isolation and proteomic workflows can be utilized to identify, quantify, and validate the presence of transporters in the rat BBB.
we have developed a workflow to quantify transporters in isolated BBB.

a combination of targeted and untargeting proteomics can be used to identify and quantify BBB proteins, which will assist in the translation of pharmacokinetic and toxicokinetic observations in rodents to humans.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of label‐free proteomics is a powerful tool to quantify proteins from isolated brain microvessles and that the use of a combination of targeted and label‐free quantification is a useful tool for quantification of proteins of interest.
the use of label‐free proteomics is an excellent method for quantification of proteins in the brain microvessel endothelial cells.
the use of multiple proteomics workflows is needed to ensure that the most comprehensive list of proteins is identified and quantified.
